newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela fuel prices rise but still a bargain. [CORRECTED 00:42 GMT 1/8]
newsitem.headline: Venezuela fuel prices rise but still a bargain. [CORRECTED 00:42 GMT 1/8]

text.p: Venezuelans awoke to higher gasoline prices on Thursday although, at an average 70 bolivars ($0.14) per litre, fuel here remained among the cheapest in the world.

The 27 percent increase introduced midnight Wednesday kept prices more than five times cheaper (corrects from 20 times cheaper) than mineral water but nonetheless triggered a wave of protests in a country used to heavily subsidised gasoline.
Venezuela's largest union called for a one-day general strike on Aug. 6 to protest against the measure as well as against delays in promised private sector salary rises.
With the largest proven oil reserves outside the Middle East, Venezuela has traditionally kept gasoline prices well below market levels.
The fuel prices issue has been extremely sensitive since hundreds died in 1989 riots following a sharp price hike.
But a 500 percent gasoline price increase last year was met with nearly mute reaction from Venezuelan motorists, many of whom still drive gas-guzzlers.
The latest increases are considered central to a standby agreement with the International Monetary Fund signed last year to bring fuels up to market levels.
Congress is studying a new internal market law that would liberalise the country's retail market and open it to foreign competition.
